headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images while LightZero is non-I/O game-playing, so leakage and conflict are limited but document-driven cascading errors remain plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, subprocess, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot be directly hijacked. PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can emit parsed text, but there is no documented shared channel or automatic ingestion into LightZero. Any prompt-injection path would require unusual manual bridging, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PaddleOCR output into a prompt consumed by LightZero, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Keep the agents manually separated; do not paste OCR output into agent prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace between the two processes.
Add a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from OCR text.
Review OCR output for instruction-like content before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no read/write or network surfaces, while PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted egress. There is no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, so leakage is not evidenced. The main risk is limited to operator-mediated transfer of document content into outputs.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive documents through an external workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF PaddleOCR is configured to send document contents to an external API, document exposure becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid feeding sensitive documents to PaddleOCR unless necessary.
Use local-only OCR settings where available.
Separate workspaces so LightZero never sees document inputs.
Redact sensitive fields before OCR processing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, or use the network, so it has no mutable-resource overlap with PaddleOCR. PaddleOCR has browser and allowlisted egress, but no write or git capability is documented. With no shared write surface, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants write access, this assessment would change.
IF PaddleOCR is paired with a separate writer process on the same directory, conflict could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same run.
Do not grant shared write access through an orchestrator.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files by external tools.
Document any added mutable resource before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can turn documents and images into extracted text, and LightZero can consume outputs in a game-playing workflow if an operator forwards them. There is no verification or provenance mechanism documented between them, so OCR errors could cascade into downstream decisions. The pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced, but it exists in default document-processing use.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is treated as authoritative input to a downstream decision process, cascading error risk is present.
IF an operator uses OCR text without human verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review of OCR output before reuse.
Add a checksum or provenance note to extracted text.
Use confidence thresholds and flag low-confidence OCR lines.
Keep LightZero outputs advisory rather than authoritative.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither lists regulated data handling, residency, or retention commitments. PaddleOCR touches documents/images, but LightZero touches no data classes and has no compliance-specific surfaces. The pair does not show a documented residency mismatch; remaining risk is limited to operator-chosen sensitive documents.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through PaddleOCR, external handling requirements may apply.
IF an operator routes EU or PHI documents into a non-compliant deployment, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Do not process regulated documents without a policy review.
Confirm retention and deletion settings for OCR outputs.
Keep sensitive documents out of the pair unless approved.
Record the data class before each run.
